text:
nora (People Ops): Quick question: candidate booked their own trip and asked for reimbursement. Also planning dinner with two interviewers; one may bring a +1. What receipts/details do we need and how do we handle guest items?

ben (Recruiting Ops): Reimburse coach fares up to the hiring cap (domestic cap $600). No per-diem for candidates. Need e-ticket/boarding pass + proof of payment. For dinners: company covers candidate portion; partner/guest is not reimbursable.

Sam (Finance): If interviewer pays personally, they can submit the receipt but must annotate candidate portion. Upload full itemized receipt + note: "Candidate - [name] - portion $X". We will not reimburse guest alcohol or non-candidate items.

Olga (Hiring Manager): If the interviewer uses company card, easier right?

ben (Recruiting Ops): Yes, company card preferred. If using company card, note attendee list in notes. If partner present, front-desk or receipt note should exclude them.

travel-bot: TravelPolicyBot: Reminder: submit candidate travel claims within 30 days. Required: e-ticket/boarding pass, proof of payment (card or receipt), itemized lodging receipt if applicable. Any claim > $2,000 needs travel@redwood approval.

nora (People Ops): Edge case: candidate stayed with friend (no invoice) and paid cash for local transit. Are these reimbursable?

Sam (Finance): Cash-only or "no invoice" lodging not reimbursable. For transit, we need a receipt; if none, a signed attestation and manager approval may be accepted for small amounts (<$50).

Olga (Hiring Manager): Thanks — I'll tell interviewers to use the company card for the dinner or take a clear photo and split the receipt when submitting.

nora (People Ops): I'll add this wording to the recruiting playbook and include a short expense template.
